title: Lehmann denies knowledge of sandpaper plot
excerpt: The former Australia coach also spoke about the mental and emotional toll of the 2018 scandal
author: Cricbuzz Staff
body: Darren Lehmann, Australia's head coach at the time of the 'Sandpapergate' scandal, has once again denied any knowledge of the plot. Speaking on ABC's broadcast during the first T20I between Australia and England, Lehmann said his “version stays the same” and reiterated that he “didn't know” sandpaper would be used.
“The biggest thing with ball tampering is [that] it was just a bad time. Everyone, we all made mistakes… We've just got to try and move on. I know it's hard for everyone,” he said.

Recent revelations by several players, including a 4,000-word piece by Cameron Bancroft in The West Australian, threw fresh light on the scandal, with Bancroft specifically alleging that Lehmann and then bowling coach David Saker had agreed to the plot during the tea break on the second day of the second Test.

“I can't remember that conversation. Again, eight and a half years ago. You'd have to ask those people… That's the issue. I have my version and that's where I stand,” said Lehmann when asked about Bancroft's account.

Lehmann, who resigned in the aftermath of the scandal, also spoke about the mental and emotional toll of the incident. “Eight and a half years ago, and I don't like talking about this sort of scenario, but I went to a really dark place. As dark a place as you can think about.

“It took me, and this is just me, probably three or four years to actually get back to some sort of normality. To the stage where we are now, I'm not going back to that. I'm trying to move forward. I'm not going back,” he said.
Describing the period as “traumatic”, Lehmann called for an end to the debate and urged people to respect the fact that “everyone's going through a tough time”.

“I feel for everyone at the moment and their families. Social media has been so vitriolic. The hatred is there. It's just unbelievable. I've never seen anything like it since 2018. And the trauma for everyone is there to see again. I know people aren't in a great place.
“Some of the things that are being said are just outright hurtful to a lot of people… Yes, there were mistakes. You apologise as best you can, you try and move on.

“I can only speak for me. I wish we did things differently and we didn't push the boundaries too far. We didn't get to the stage where we got to. I've just got to take responsibility for that. That's where I'm at,” he added.
